doc: Semantics a port must reproduce (verified by an independent direct convolution with no scipy: it agrees to 5.8e-8 on every smoothing case): each row is filtered along longitude with its own sigma s = min(w/4, sigma_km / (px_km max(cos lat, 1e-3))) pixels, px_km = 2 pi R / w, only when s > 0.3 (otherwise the row is copied); then every column is filtered with sigma_km / px_km. scipy gaussian_filter1d: kernel taps -r..r with r = int(4 s + 0.5), weights exp(-0.5 x^2 / s^2) normalized to sum 1, accumulated in float64 and rounded to float32 once per pass; mode "wrap" is periodic (indices modulo w, even when r >= w), mode "nearest" repeats the edge row. A tall 8-column x 1700-row field: the half-texel pole rows have cos(lat) = 9.2e-4 < 1e-3, so the floor max(cos, 1e-3) engages on the first and last row only. sigma 2 km on Earth: every row has sigma 4e-4 px (copied) except those two, whose sigma is 0.40 px with the floor (0.43 without it: they differ by up to 0.03 in value, so the case is sensitive to the floor); the column pass has r = 0 (identity). Default tolerance. params.constants lists the module constants and the inline numbers the function reads (a port copies them from its own source and may assert that they equal these).
